name: com.criptonlabs/agent-apis
title: Criptonlabs Agent APIs
description: Read-only XRPL and Solana data for agents: fees, slippage, readiness. Free /mcp; x402 /mcp/pro.

tools.name: xrpl_fee
tools.description: Current XRPL fee tiers in drops with a congestion score. When to use: Before submitting a transaction, to choose a `Fee` and to decide whether the network is congested. Prefer another tool: Not a price feed and not a historical series; it describes the current open ledger only. Example: xrpl_fee {}

tools.name: xrpl_network_health
tools.description: Overall and per-node health of the upstream XRPL nodes. When to use: To decide whether to trust or retry data, or to explain a 503 from another endpoint. Prefer another tool: Not a probe of your own connectivity; it reports the service's upstream nodes. Example: xrpl_network_health {}

tools.name: xrpl_orderbook
tools.description: CLOB order book for a currency pair with unfunded offers removed. When to use: To read executable liquidity for a pair on the XRPL central limit order book (CLOB). Prefer another tool: Not for AMM liquidity (use the amm page) and not for a cost estimate (use the slippage page). Example: xrpl_orderbook {"base":"XRP","quote":"USD.rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"}

base.description: Base currency: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

quote.description: Quote currency: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

depth.description: Levels per side: a positive integer no larger than 9007199254740991, rounded up to 10, 50 or 100; a larger depth is served at 100 (see depth_effective)

domain.description: Optional PermissionedDomain id (64 hex): reads that domain's permissioned order book; slippage then skips the AMM

tools.name: xrpl_slippage
tools.description: Slippage and average price for buying or selling an amount of base currency. When to use: Before placing a market-style trade, to size it against available depth and to see whether the CLOB or the AMM pool gives the better average price for the side. Prefer another tool: It is an estimate, not a quote, and it does not split an amount across venues or route through other pairs. To read pool reserves, use the amm page. Example: xrpl_slippage {"base":"XRP","quote":"USD.rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B","amount":"1000"}

base.description: Base currency: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

quote.description: Quote currency: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

amount.description: Positive decimal amount of base to buy or sell

depth.description: Levels per side: a positive integer no larger than 9007199254740991, rounded up to 10, 50 or 100; a larger depth is served at 100 (default 100)

side.description: Trade direction: buy walks the asks (pays quote for amount of base), sell walks the bids (sells amount of base for quote)

domain.description: Optional PermissionedDomain id (64 hex): reads that domain's permissioned order book; slippage then skips the AMM

tools.name: xrpl_amm
tools.description: AMM pool reserves and trading fee for an asset pair. When to use: To read AMM pool depth and fee for a pair. Prefer another tool: It does not estimate slippage or compare venues (use the slippage page for the CLOB vs AMM comparison); a pair without a pool returns 404. Example: xrpl_amm {"a":"XRP","b":"4555524F50000000000000000000000000000000.rMkEuRii9w9uBMQDnWV5AA43gvYZR9JxVK"}

a.description: First asset: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

b.description: Second asset: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: xrpl_account_summary
tools.description: XRP balance, sequence, owner count, transfer rate and trust lines (capped) for an account. When to use: To inspect an account before building a transaction for it. Prefer another tool: Not for transaction history or reserves; it is a summary, not a full account dump. Example: xrpl_account_summary {"address":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"}

address.description: Valid classic XRPL account address (r..., checksum verified)

tools.name: xrpl_account_lines
tools.description: One page of an account's trust lines, with an opaque cursor for the next page. When to use: To list every trust line of an account (balances, limits, freeze and authorization flags), page by page. Prefer another tool: For a quick capped overview with the XRP balance, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`; for issued totals of a token, use the token endpoint. Example: xrpl_account_lines {"address":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"}

address.description: Valid classic XRPL account address (r..., checksum verified)

limit.description: Lines per page: an integer from 10 to 400 (default 100)

peer.description: Only lines with this counterparty (classic address)

marker.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `marker`, for the same address

tools.name: xrpl_account_transactions
tools.description: One page of an account's most recent validated transactions, newest first. When to use: To check what an account did recently (payments sent or received, offers, trust line changes) and whether each transaction succeeded. Prefer another tool: For balances and trust lines, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`; for full archival history, use a full-history node or indexer: history depth depends on the serving node and older pages may be slower. Example: xrpl_account_transactions {"address":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"}

address.description: Valid classic XRPL account address (r..., checksum verified)

limit.description: Transactions per page: an integer from 1 to 50 (default 20)

marker.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `marker`, for the same address

tools.name: xrpl_token
tools.description: Issuer data for an issued asset: flags, domain, transfer fee and total issued. When to use: Before accepting or sending an issued token: check that the issuer exists, is not frozen, whether holders need authorization, and the transfer fee charged on every transfer between non-issuer accounts. Prefer another tool: For XRP (not an issued asset; 400), for one account's own balances use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`, and for prices use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`. Example: xrpl_token {"asset":"USD.rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"}

asset.description: Issued asset, never XRP. Currency format: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: xrpl_payment_readiness
tools.description: Pre-payment check: can this payment from source to destination succeed now? When to use: Right before sending a payment: to catch a missing or unfunded destination, a required destination tag, deposit authorization, missing or frozen trust lines, MPT authorization and locks, insufficient balance and issuer freezes, in one call. Prefer another tool: To find a multi-hop route or the source amount needed for a cross-currency payment (use the paths endpoint), or to list balances (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`). Example: xrpl_payment_readiness {"source":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B","destination":"rhub8VRN55s94qWKDv6jmDy1pUykJzF3wq"}

source.description: Sending account: valid classic XRPL address (r..., checksum verified)

destination.description: Receiving account: valid classic XRPL address, different from source

asset.description: Asset to deliver; default XRP. `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code. Or a 48-hex MPT issuance id (hex letters in either case), with `amount` in whole base units.

amount.description: Positive decimal amount of asset (whole base units for an MPT); omit to skip amount-dependent checks

destination_tag.description: Destination tag you will send: an integer from 0 to 4294967295

credentials.description: Comma-separated Credential entry IDs (1 to 8, 64 hex); checked with deposit_authorized

tools.name: xrpl_paths
tools.description: Multi-hop payment paths and their source cost. When to use: Before a cross-currency or multi-hop payment: to see whether a route exists and how much the source would spend to deliver the amount. A call can take up to about 20 seconds and paths may be non-optimal. Prefer another tool: To check whether a direct payment can succeed (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or for the single-hop cost of a trade on one pair (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`, which compares the order book and the AMM). Example: xrpl_paths {"source":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B","destination":"rhub8VRN55s94qWKDv6jmDy1pUykJzF3wq","asset":"XRP","amount":"1"}

source.description: Sending account: valid classic XRPL address (r..., checksum verified)

destination.description: Receiving account: valid classic XRPL address

asset.description: Asset delivered: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

amount.description: Positive decimal amount of asset the destination receives

send_max_asset.description: Asset of send_max; give it with send_max. `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

send_max.description: Most the source may spend, in send_max_asset; not with source_assets

source_assets.description: Comma-separated assets the source may spend (1 to 4); not with send_max. Each asset: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: xrpl_latest_ledger
tools.description: Latest validated ledger index, hash and close time. When to use: To anchor other readings to a ledger or to check how current the network view is. Prefer another tool: Not for transaction data or account state; use the account endpoint for those. Example: xrpl_latest_ledger {}

tools.name: xrpl_mpt
tools.description: MPT issuance: issuer, supply, scale, transfer fee and flags. When to use: Before accepting or sending an MPT: to check its issuer, decimal scale, supply against its maximum, transfer fee, and whether it can be transferred, locked, escrowed or clawed back. Prefer another tool: To check whether one MPT payment between two accounts can succeed now (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness` with the issuance id as `asset`), or for a trust-line token written `CODE.issuer` (use `/v1/xrpl/token/{asset}`). Example: xrpl_mpt {"mpt_issuance_id":"05FA6AB8561E39FA605779B829BB5974E82B40AF173D6AF3"}

mpt_issuance_id.description: MPT issuance id: 48 hexadecimal characters, either case

tools.name: xrpl_address_kind
tools.description: What kind of XRPL address is this, and what does a payment to it need? When to use: Before paying or listing an XRPL address: to learn whether it exists, whether it is a pseudo-account that rejects payments, and whether a payment needs a destination tag or deposit preauthorization. Prefer another tool: To check one payment end to end with amounts, trust lines and reserves (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or to read balances (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`). Example: xrpl_address_kind {"address":"rhWTXC2m2gGGA9WozUaoMm6kLAVPb1tcS3"}

address.description: Valid classic XRPL account address (r..., checksum verified)

tools.name: xrpl_stablecoin
tools.description: Is this XRPL issued currency the canonical stablecoin it claims to be? When to use: Before accepting or quoting a stablecoin: to check the asset is the canonical one and that its issuer facts have not changed since the snapshot. Prefer another tool: To read supply or balances (use `/v1/xrpl/token/{asset}` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`), or as a regulatory or licensing check: none is served. Example: xrpl_stablecoin {"asset":"4555524F50000000000000000000000000000000.rMkEuRii9w9uBMQDnWV5AA43gvYZR9JxVK"}

asset.description: Issued asset, never XRP. Currency format: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: xrpl_payment_verify
tools.description: Did this settled payment deliver the expected asset and amount to the expected account? When to use: After a payment has been submitted: to confirm from the ledger that it delivered the asset and amount you expected to the account you expected, including the partial-payment case. Prefer another tool: Before sending a payment (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or to list an account's recent payments (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/transactions`). Example: xrpl_payment_verify {"hash":"002C12C53476173ABC1001505C40A24CCC90F642480C924C1B748E339FA1B069","destination":"rfaecmugiPaAkFpBT9Bmq8f3n42oXe6m1C","asset":"XRP","amount":"0.00001"}

hash.description: Transaction hash of the payment to verify: 64 hexadecimal characters

destination.description: Account the payment had to reach: valid classic XRPL address (r..., checksum verified)

asset.description: Asset the payment had to deliver. `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code. Or a 48-hex MPT issuance id (hex letters in either case), with `amount` in whole base units.

amount.description: Positive decimal amount of asset the payment had to deliver (at most 6 decimals for XRP, whole base units for an MPT)

destination_tag.description: Destination tag the payment had to carry: an integer from 0 to 4294967295; omit to skip the tag check

source.description: Account the payment had to come from; omit to skip the sender check

last_ledger_sequence.description: The LastLedgerSequence the payer signed: an integer from 1 to 4294967295; pass it for a definitive answer when the transaction is absent

tools.name: xrpl_x402_preflight
tools.description: Can this payer settle this x402 payment requirement right now? When to use: After an x402 server answered 402 with an XRPL `exact` requirement: to check, before signing, that this payer can settle that exact requirement to that recipient now. Prefer another tool: For a payment that is not an x402 requirement (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`), or once the payment has settled (use `/v1/xrpl/payment/verify`). Example: xrpl_x402_preflight {"asset":"XRP","amount":"10000000","pay_to":"rhub8VRN55s94qWKDv6jmDy1pUykJzF3wq","payer":"rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B"}

asset.description: Asset of the x402 requirement: XRP, or the currency code of an issued asset (3 characters, case-sensitive, or 40 hexadecimal characters) whose issuer goes in issuer. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens.

issuer.description: Issuer of the asset (extra.issuer of the requirement): a valid classic XRPL address; required unless the asset is XRP

amount.description: Amount the requirement asks for: a whole number of drops for XRP, a positive decimal in token units for an issued asset

pay_to.description: Account the requirement pays: valid classic XRPL address

payer.description: Wallet that would pay: valid classic XRPL address (r..., checksum verified)

destination_tag.description: Destination tag the requirement states (extra.destinationTag): an integer from 0 to 4294967295; it is passed to the readiness check

tools.name: xrpl_domain_eligibility
tools.description: Is this account a member of this XRPL permissioned domain, as its owner or through an accepted, unexpired credential? When to use: Before trading in a permissioned order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/slippage` with `domain`): to check whether an account is a member of the domain, as its owner or through an accepted, unexpired credential, and which credential qualifies it. Prefer another tool: To check whether one payment can succeed now (use `/v1/xrpl/payment-readiness`, whose `credentials` takes the `credential_id` values of this answer), or to read the permissioned order book itself (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` with `domain`). Example: xrpl_domain_eligibility {"domain_id":"DBABFD44A80DB623522628550B270FA5E2A845341E137530728E2E3699181A4E","account":"rcKV6taNcBAi8GxudZnMdFUPcH3Ls5TAv"}

domain_id.description: PermissionedDomain id: 64 hexadecimal characters, either case

account.description: Account to check as a member of the domain: valid classic XRPL address (r..., checksum verified)

tools.name: xrpl_account_offers
tools.description: One page of an account's open DEX offers, with how funded each one is. When to use: To see which DEX offers an account has open and whether each can still execute: before cancelling or replacing offers, or to check how much of an account's open offers its balances back. Prefer another tool: To read the order book of a pair (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or estimate the cost of a trade (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`); for the account's balances and trust lines, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`. Example: xrpl_account_offers {"address":"rGAs3npYy1VwLPE92kvKvA2QYLR6FSA9n6"}

address.description: Valid classic XRPL account address (r..., checksum verified)

limit.description: Offers per page: an integer from 10 to 50 (default 20)

marker.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `marker`, for the same address

tools.name: xrpl_account_commitments
tools.description: An account's escrows, payment channels and checks by direction, its deposit preauthorizations, tickets and owner reserve, and what blocks deleting it. When to use: Before deleting or winding down an account: to see which escrows can be finished or cancelled now, how much XRP is left in its payment channels, which checks expire soon, how much XRP its owned objects lock in reserve, and which owned entries block AccountDelete. Prefer another tool: To list the open DEX offers and how funded each one is (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/offers`) or the trust lines (use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`); for the balance and owner count, use `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/summary`. Example: xrpl_account_commitments {"address":"rGAs3npYy1VwLPE92kvKvA2QYLR6FSA9n6"}

address.description: Valid classic XRPL account address (r..., checksum verified)

tools.name: xrpl_metrics_pressure
tools.description: Buy or sell pressure of a pair's funded order book: a score from 0 to 100 and its band, from the depth near mid. When to use: To measure how the funded depth near mid of a pair's order book is split between bids and asks, as one score with its band. Prefer another tool: To read the order book levels (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`), the cost of a trade of a given size, CLOB against AMM (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`), or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Example: xrpl_metrics_pressure {"base":"XRP","quote":"5553444300000000000000000000000000000000.rGm7WCVp9gb4jZHWTEtGUr4dd74z2XuWhE"}

base.description: Base currency of the book: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

quote.description: Quote currency of the book, different from base: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: xrpl_metrics_peg
tools.description: How far a registry stablecoin trades from its peg on the XRP Ledger DEX: the deviation of each price route, their median and a status. When to use: To check, from the XRP Ledger's own order books and AMM pools, how far a registry stablecoin trades from its peg against another registry coin, and how much funded depth sits near the peg. Prefer another tool: To check that an issued currency is the canonical registry coin, or to read its issuer posture (use `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}`); for an asset outside the registry, which this route refuses, read its order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or its AMM pool (`/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Example: xrpl_metrics_peg {"asset":"524C555344000000000000000000000000000000.rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De"}

asset.description: XRPL stablecoin of the registry whose peg is measured, by its canonical code and issuer: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

against.description: USD stablecoin of the registry, other than asset, it is priced in; omit for the peg default (the other USD registry coin for a USD asset, RLUSD for an EUR asset): `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: xrpl_metrics_fx_basis
tools.description: The EUR/USD rate the XRP Ledger DEX implies through the EUR registry stablecoin against each USD registry stablecoin, and its basis to the ECB reference rate. When to use: To measure, from the XRP Ledger's own order books and AMM pools, the EUR/USD rate the DEX implies through the EUR registry stablecoin against each USD registry stablecoin, and how far it sits from the ECB reference rate. Prefer another tool: To measure how far one registry stablecoin trades from its peg against another registry coin (use `/v1/xrpl/metrics/peg`), or to read an order book or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook` or `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Example: xrpl_metrics_fx_basis {}

tools.name: xrpl_metrics_arbitrage
tools.description: Whether a pair's AMM pool and its order book are apart after the AMM fee: per direction the gap, the executable size and the profit after transfer fees. When to use: To find whether a pair's AMM pool and its funded order book are apart after the AMM fee, in which direction, how much base the gap allows and the profit after transfer fees, optionally with the cycles of the USD registry stablecoins via XRP. Prefer another tool: To estimate the cost of a trade of a given size, CLOB against AMM (use `/v1/xrpl/slippage`), or to read the order book levels (use `/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or an AMM pool (use `/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`); the answer measures the ledger and is not an executable quote. Example: xrpl_metrics_arbitrage {"base":"XRP","quote":"524C555344000000000000000000000000000000.rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De"}

base.description: Base currency of the pair: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

quote.description: Quote currency of the pair, different from base: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

include_triangles.description: The string "true" adds the cycles of the USD registry coins (RLUSD, USDC) via XRP; "false" or omitted leaves them out

tools.name: xrpl_metrics_liquidity_stress
tools.description: How stressed a registry stablecoin's liquidity is against its peg default: a score from 0 to 100, its band and the four weighted components behind it. When to use: To score, from the XRP Ledger's own order books, AMM pool and issuer account, how stressed a registry stablecoin's liquidity is against its peg default, as one score with its band and the components behind it. Prefer another tool: To read the peg deviation of each price route (use `/v1/xrpl/metrics/peg`), or to check that an issued currency is the canonical registry coin and read its issuer posture (use `/v1/xrpl/stablecoin/{asset}`); for an asset outside the registry, which this route refuses, read its order book (`/v1/xrpl/orderbook`) or its AMM pool (`/v1/xrpl/amm/{a}/{b}`). Example: xrpl_metrics_liquidity_stress {"asset":"524C555344000000000000000000000000000000.rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De"}

asset.description: XRPL stablecoin of the registry whose liquidity stress is measured against its peg default, by its canonical code and issuer: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.

tools.name: solana_transfer_readiness
tools.description: Will this Solana transfer succeed? A verdict for SOL or an SPL or Token-2022 token. When to use: Before building or signing a Solana transfer, to learn whether it will fail and what it will cost in rent and fees. Prefer another tool: Not a simulation of the exact transaction (no priority fee, no program logic), not a token price or holder lookup, and not a way to read raw accounts. Example: solana_transfer_readiness {"source":"83astBRguLMdt2h5U1Tpdq5tjFoJ6noeGwaY3mDLVcri","destination":"A1TMhSGzQxMr1TboBKtgixKz1sS6REASMxPo1qsyTSJd","mint":"SOL","amount":"0.5"}

source.description: Sending wallet: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

destination.description: Receiving wallet (not its token account), different from source: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

mint.description: `SOL` for native SOL, or the mint address of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token

amount.description: Positive decimal amount in UI units (SOL or tokens, not lamports or raw units); at most 18446744073709551615 in raw units

tools.name: solana_token
tools.description: Is this Solana token safe to hold or receive? A safe, warn or danger verdict. When to use: Before accepting or swapping into an unfamiliar token, to see whether its mint can freeze, mint more, move or tax balances. Prefer another tool: Not a price, liquidity or holder lookup and not an audit of the token's project; it reads only the mint account. Example: solana_token {"mint":"EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v"}

mint.description: Mint address of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token (base58, 32 bytes)

tools.name: solana_latest_slot
tools.description: Latest finalized Solana slot and its block time. When to use: To check how fresh the finalized view of Solana is, or to anchor a read to a slot. Prefer another tool: Not a tip-of-chain feed: it is finalized, not processed or confirmed, and it is cached for 2 seconds. Example: solana_latest_slot {}

tools.name: solana_network_health
tools.description: Whether Solana data is currently being served: latest probe status and finalized slot. When to use: Before relying on the Solana verdict endpoints, or to explain a 503 from them. Prefer another tool: Not a measure of the Solana network itself, only of this service's access to it; use the latest-slot endpoint to see chain progress. Example: solana_network_health {}

tools.name: solana_fee_readiness
tools.description: Can this Solana account pay the fees of N transactions now? When to use: Before sending one or more transactions from a wallet: to learn whether it can pay their base fees without dropping below its rent-exempt minimum. Prefer another tool: To check one SOL or token transfer end to end (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to read a balance (none is returned). Example: solana_fee_readiness {"address":"83astBRguLMdt2h5U1Tpdq5tjFoJ6noeGwaY3mDLVcri"}

address.description: Fee-payer account: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

transaction_count.description: Number of transactions to pay for: integer from 1 to 1000; default 1

signatures.description: Signatures per transaction: integer from 1 to 10; default 1

tools.name: solana_token_hygiene
tools.description: Which of this wallet's Solana token accounts can be closed for rent, or are delegated or frozen? When to use: Before cleaning up a wallet: to learn how much rent closing its empty token accounts returns, and whether any token account has an active delegate or is frozen. Prefer another tool: To list token accounts, mints or balances (none are returned), or to check one transfer end to end (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`). Example: solana_token_hygiene {"address":"83astBRguLMdt2h5U1Tpdq5tjFoJ6noeGwaY3mDLVcri"}

address.description: Owner wallet whose token accounts are scanned: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

tools.name: solana_address_kind
tools.description: What kind of Solana account is this address, and should a payment go to it? When to use: Before sending SOL or tokens to an address: to learn whether it is a wallet, a token account (and whose), a mint, a program or another program-owned account. Prefer another tool: To check one transfer end to end with amounts and fees (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to read balances (none are returned). Example: solana_address_kind {"address":"Ffeie177PRngys3SwNH44AYdT9yExm63GAmTXHdmL1k1"}

address.description: Address to classify: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

tools.name: solana_stablecoin
tools.description: Is this Solana mint the canonical stablecoin it claims to be? When to use: Before accepting or quoting a stablecoin: to check the mint is the canonical one and that its mint facts have not changed since the snapshot. Prefer another tool: To read supply or balances (use `/v1/solana/token/{mint}`), or as a regulatory or licensing check: none is served. Example: solana_stablecoin {"mint":"2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo"}

mint.description: Mint address of an SPL Token or Token-2022 token (base58, 32 bytes)

tools.name: solana_payment_verify
tools.description: Did this settled Solana payment deliver the expected amount to the expected recipient? When to use: After a payment has been submitted: to confirm from the chain that the recipient received the mint and amount you expected, including the Token-2022 fee case. Prefer another tool: Before sending a transfer (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or to list a wallet's transfers or balances (none are returned). Example: solana_payment_verify {"signature":"B7yABUkY4RudiDfoax94mfqVv2YuNJ4AVsg7LjdFT9Qm8bScsw3PoB2LxpuUqzCkiniKQJ9AKXfSfWaw1kWYFaF","recipient":"GEJySUi6LjHwQWKD2BDg3TiGKwhKmBU7JJTjZfk1RD54","mint":"SOL","amount":"0.02"}

signature.description: Transaction signature of the payment to verify: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 64 bytes

recipient.description: Wallet the payment had to reach (not its token account): Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

mint.description: `SOL` for native SOL, or the mint address of the SPL Token or Token-2022 token the payment had to deliver

amount.description: Positive decimal amount the payment had to deliver, in UI units (not lamports or raw units); at most 9 decimals for SOL

reference.description: Reference key the payment had to carry among its account keys: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes; omit to skip the reference check

source.description: Wallet the payment had to be signed by: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes; omit to skip the sender check

tools.name: solana_x402_preflight
tools.description: Can this payer settle this x402 payment requirement right now? When to use: After an x402 server answered 402 with a Solana `exact` requirement: to check, before signing, that this payer can settle that exact requirement to that recipient now. Prefer another tool: For a transfer that is not an x402 requirement (use `/v1/solana/transfer-readiness`), or once the payment has settled (use `/v1/solana/payment/verify`). Example: solana_x402_preflight {"asset":"2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo","amount":"1000000","pay_to":"29d2S7vB453rNYFdR5Ycwt7y9haRT5fwVwL9zTmBhfV2","payer":"6vk7icY2FzdMTzMGE4aNRSzovanAmS7xsv9uHwj4YuzY"}

asset.description: Mint of the x402 requirement: the token the payment moves (base58, 32 bytes); `SOL` is not accepted, because an x402 SVM `exact` payment is always a token transfer

amount.description: Amount the requirement asks for, in the mint's base units (not UI units): a whole number of digits, at most 18446744073709551615

pay_to.description: Wallet the requirement pays (not its token account): Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes

payer.description: Wallet that would pay: Solana wallet address: a base58 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes
